extracted.intended_audience: people asking mathematics questions on Mathematics Stack Exchange (Math.SE) / users who want to improve their question quality
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing clear, answerable mathematics questions suitable for the Mathematics Stack Exchange site so they will receive helpful answers from the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you thoroughly searched for an answer before asking your question? Sharing your research helps everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell us what you found and why it didn’t meet your needs. This demonstrates that you’ve taken the time to try to help yourself, it saves us from reiterating obvious answers, and above all, it helps you get a more specific and relevant answer!

rubrics_metrics.name: Be on-topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask only about topics defined by the community's on-topic guidance; avoid asking for opinions or open-ended discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can view the set of topics in the help center; if your question is about the site itself, ask on the meta-discussion site. If you’re looking for a different topic, it might be covered on another Stack Exchange site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details and context so your question is not vague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you ask a vague question, you’ll get a vague answer. Giving details and context lets responders provide a useful answer (include definitions, what you’ve tried, precise statements of the problem, any constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make it relevant to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the question so it is useful to more than just yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it clear how your question is relevant to more people than just you; broader relevance encourages more users to be interested and willing to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep an open mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to receive answers you didn’t expect or that don’t match your preferred solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer may not always be the one you wanted, and a conclusive answer isn’t always possible. When in doubt, ask answerers to cite sources or explain how/where they learned something. Even if you disagree, remember responders are trying to help.
